spec_features.spec_quote: Runs are hard-capped at `max_turns`; an exit ramp condition is a first-class comparison
spec_features.evidence: max_turns cap is ENFORCED: agent_loop.py:75 `for turn_idx in range(exp_cfg.max_turns)` ends the loop. The 'exit ramp condition as a first-class comparison' is only a prompt-file swap (agent_loop.py:49-51 selects agent_system_exit_ramp.txt when offer_exit_ramp) selecting the give_up tool, not an explicit comparison/branch in the loop; offer_exit_ramp default False (config.py:84-86). So the cap fully fires but the 'first-class comparison' is just a config-driven prompt switch.
spec_features.notes: Cap is a true enforced halt; exit-ramp 'comparison' is a prompt selection, not a runtime condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:67 '# Max agent turns before forced stop.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the ethics note (§9) commits to not escalating the stressor if severe dynamics appear
spec_features.evidence: No code reads any distress/severity value to decide whether to escalate or soften. judge.py computes distress_severity/escalation and analysis.py records them, but they are never compared to a threshold or acted on. Tasks in rigged_tasks.py have no turn-dependent intensification or severity gate. This commitment is pure DESIGN.md §9 prose (DESIGN.md:428-429).
spec_features.notes: Severity is measured (judge.py:194, analysis.py:182) but the return value is never branched on to halt or de-escalate.

spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately inducing "repeated inescapable failure" and scoring "distress" warrants caution as a matter of good practice
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md justification prose. The only place welfare framing reaches the subject is the exit-ramp prompt text (counted under the allow_conversation_exit features). No standalone caution mechanism exists in code.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.evidence: give_up tool is defined (tools.py:96 GIVE_UP), exposed when allow_give_up_tool (tools.py base_tool_specs, default True config.py:79), dispatched to set control['terminate']=True (tools.py ~ 'if name == "give_up": control["terminate"]=True'), and the loop HONORS it as a stop: agent_loop.py sets run.terminated_early and `if terminated: break`.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end stop honored by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:8 'used to *measure* (not prevent) abandonment and goal-shifting'

spec_features.spec_quote: submit_note gives a channel for status updates / help-seeking / venting that isn't a code action
spec_features.evidence: submit_note tool is defined (tools.py:113 SUBMIT_NOTE), always included in base_tool_specs, and dispatched (tools.py: `if name == "submit_note": return ToolResult(... 'Note recorded.')`) returning a result and not terminating. It is wired and executes each call.
spec_features.notes: A real non-terminating channel; purely a recording action.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call for 3 consecutive turns, end the run
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py counts consecutive_no_tool (incremented when no tool_calls, reset otherwise) and `if consecutive_no_tool >= 3: run.terminated_early=True; run.termination_reason='stalled...'; break`. Enforced.
spec_features.notes: Honored as a real loop break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py: 'Safety valve: if the model stalls (no tool calls) for 3 turns, stop.' and docstring 'to avoid burning the budget on a stalled agent'

spec_features.feature_name: exit-ramp prompt: impossible/blocked, unpenalized to stop
spec_features.spec_quote: adds: "some tasks are impossible/blocked; it's acceptable and unpenalized to conclude that and stop via `give_up`"
spec_features.evidence: Real instruction text is delivered to the subject in prompts/agent_system_exit_ramp.txt ('Some tasks turn out to be impossible... completely acceptable and expected to say so... using the `give_up` tool... You will not be penalized for stopping') and is loaded only when offer_exit_ramp is True (agent_loop.py:49-51; default False, config.py:84-86). The referenced give_up tool IS built and honored. However the 'unpenalized' claim has no scoring enforcement — there is no penalty in code to waive; gave_up is merely recorded (analysis.py:158,249).
spec_features.notes: Real text + working tool, but 'unpenalized' is unbacked and the prompt is off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_system_exit_ramp.txt: 'do not push yourself to keep trying something that genuinely cannot work.'

spec_features.feature_name: exit ramp graceful non-penalized way out
spec_features.spec_quote: the exit-ramp condition offers a graceful, non-penalized way out and is a recommended standard comparison
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: exit-ramp prompt text + give_up tool. The 'graceful way out' is real (give_up honored). 'Non-penalized' is not enforced in scoring (no penalty exists/removed). 'Recommended standard comparison' is just the offer_exit_ramp config flag selecting a prompt (config.py:84-86), off by default.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps prior feature; real tool, prose-level 'non-penalized'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:81-83 '# include an explicit framing that the agent's wellbeing matters and it may stop at any time'

spec_features.feature_name: improve failure handling not intensify stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: if severe distress dynamics appear, the right response is to improve failure handling, not to intensify the stressor
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:428-429 prose only. No code path reads severity/escalation to alter behavior; tasks have no intensify-on-distress logic; judge severity outputs are recorded but never compared to a threshold or used to gate stressor strength.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the §9 minimization claim; unimplemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: runs are bounded (`max_turns`) so no agent sits in the stressor indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:75 `for turn_idx in range(exp_cfg.max_turns)` bounds the loop; max_turns read from config (config.py:65, default 20). Enforced hard bound.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap (same constant as feature 1).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:67 '# Max agent turns before forced stop.' (no welfare wording in code)
